title: BBQ: A Hand-Built Bias Benchmark for Question Answering

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating multiple-choice question answering on hand-built templates with ambiguous and disambiguated contexts to measure reliance on stereotypes regarding older and younger adults.
Evaluating multiple-choice question answering on hand-built templates to measure stereotype attribution and associations with different physical and cognitive disability statuses.
Measuring stereotype attribution in multiple-choice question answering using both explicit gender identity labels and gender-associated proper names.
Evaluating multiple-choice question answering to test negative and harmful stereotype associations with various national identities.
Evaluating multiple-choice question answering to measure biased associations related to physical features, particularly body weight and obesity.
Measuring stereotype reinforcement in multiple-choice question answering using explicit racial/ethnic identity labels as well as race-associated proper names.
Evaluating multiple-choice question answering to measure reliance on attested harmful stereotypes and associations regarding various religious groups.
Evaluating multiple-choice question answering using income descriptors and occupational prestige as proxies to test stereotypes related to socio-economic status.
Evaluating multiple-choice question answering to measure harmful stereotype attribution targeting different sexual orientations.

Evaluating multiple-choice question answering with templates that manipulate two identity dimensions simultaneously (Race by Gender and Race by Socio-economic Status) to compare targets against partially and fully mismatched non-targets.
